body:
Hi @Ladicek Thanks for the above, re 3., I did see `leeway` was being used in `Vertx` but since at a time I was dealing with the user request to do with the the expiration grace I called it as such :-).
I think to address `3` properly we'd also need to introduce `not-before` check which is also done by Vertx during the token verification
I'm also thinking if perhaps the default leeway should be > 0, WDYT? I'm no security expert, but clock skew of about 10 seconds is not unheard of, I'd say.

issue.title: OIDC expiration-grace property name is misleading
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
As noted in #8469, `quarkus.oidc.token.expiration-grace` is misleading. I originally named it this way because I thought the Vertx `leeway` property was only about the expiration grace but it is effectively a lifespan grace.

Proposal is to rename it now to avoid any confusions going forward, effectively `quarkus.oidc.token.expiration-grace` name is a bug

body:
@Ladicek Regarding documentation, you are right. However, the reason why we don't have more references in `quarkus-keycloak-authorization` extension is that I did not want to replicate what we have in the Keycloak Authorization Services [documentation](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/authorization_services/index.html#_enforcer_filter).

The extension is basically exposing the Keycloak Policy Enforcer to Quarkus application. All configuration you can do there you can have in Quarkus. Yeah, we are talking about properties vs json, so for certain configuration options (like the path config) is not so obvious how to map them to Quarkus.

That said, I'm not sure about replicating all the config there into Quarkus docs. But maybe we can describe better some very common usages and use cases like this one for disabling policy enforcement for a specific path?

Regarding the clock skew, we have that for SAML but not for OIDC. Not sure why, we should probably include that.

@pedroigor I'd say "is not so obvious" is an understatement. One, I had no clue this mirrors some Keycloak configuration that I could look at. Two, I had to step through the `quarkus-keycloak-authorization` extension code _in a debugger (!)_ to find these configuration options and how to use them.

Given that Quarkus has (wants to have) a monopoly on configuration, the properties must be documented. The autogenerated documentation should cost you nothing. Adding an example or two would be good for sure.

@Ladicek You are right. We can definitely include the config options as we have for other extensions.

I'm going to update docs to make more clear the extension is related to Keycloak Policy Enforcer as well as add the config options.
